tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

# @notary/web

Read-only Notary dashboard built with React, Vite, Tailwind, shadcn/ui primitives
and Dither Kit. The home page is Overview; Queue, Beliefs, Probe log, Runs
comparison, Economics and Evidence share its visual system. Geist uses light and
regular weights. Warm neutral surfaces, a blue accent and SVG diagonal hatching
separate focus and baseline series. Green/red are reserved for safety deltas.

## Local development

The web app is part of the pnpm workspace; the root `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the only
lockfile. From the repo root:

```powershell
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --filter @notary/web dev
pnpm --filter @notary/web typecheck
pnpm --filter @notary/web test
pnpm --filter @notary/web build
```

`dist` is the static output; Vite serves `public` assets unchanged. The app imports
`packages/core/src/schema` and `packages/core/src/bundle/hash.ts` from source, so the
whole workspace (including `packages/core` and its `zod`) must be installed to build.

## Integrity and data sources

The catalog reads `public/bundles/index.json` and the optional
`public/bundles/fixture/index.json`. Every listed bundle must pass the shared core
schema, a browser-recomputed content hash and index metadata checks before any
catalog data is rendered. A corrupt bundle, mislabeled fixture or
`x-notary-hash-mismatch: 1` withholds the catalog and displays a visible error.
The fixture directory rejects bundles whose `sample` flag is false.

Run selection defaults to a guarded queue run when available. The baseline
picker permits only the same fixture/live cohort. Charts never combine those
cohorts. Navigating to Probe log chooses a bundle with probes if the current run
has none; returning to a queue screen chooses a guarded queue run. The selected
run is always identified in the picker. Overview's experimental coverage can
use a same-cohort notarization bundle and explicitly names that source.

The fixture banner stays visible while scrolling. Evidence keeps integration
receipts and the fixture comparison in separate sections, including when a live
run is selected. Required tool content comes from
`public/evidence/evidence.json`; omitted tools show Pending. Optional
`public/economics.json` is shown as the cfo.ai plan; otherwise the screen shows
"cfo.ai plan pending".

Numbers are bundle fields, JSON fields or computations over them. Missing
metrics remain unknown, rather than becoming zero. Model USD is summed from
`usageByRole`; API credits are never given an invented USD exchange rate.
Zero-cost roles are listed explicitly. A cost per belief with no notarized
beliefs is undefined. The safety takeaway describes recorded differences and
held refunds without claiming live causation.

Queue flow counts requests, distinct decided request IDs and individual terminal
outcomes. Executed/held/escalated are sibling branches, not successive funnel
conversions; tooltips show signed differences between adjacent counts. Belief
categories are disjoint: notarized above/below neutral confidence, abstained,
adversary-downgraded and unresolved. Confidence means P(documentation holds).

Trace links come exclusively from bundle receipts; absent links show recorded
IDs. Local JSONL receipt links require the run files to be hosted separately.
Fixtures and example URLs do not demonstrate live tracing. Live API/SSE and a
Vercel deployment remain separate scheduled work in TASKS.md.

## Visual quality checks

With the local dev server running and Chrome installed:

```powershell
$env:NOTARY_PREVIEW_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:5173'
npm run check:visual
```

Playwright captures all seven pages in light/dark mode at desktop and phone
widths, plus detail views. Artifacts go to ignored `screenshots/U4`; set
`NOTARY_SCREENSHOTS` to change the output directory. The script checks page
headings, theme, persistent fixture disclosure, horizontal overflow, browser
errors and visible rejection of a tampered bundle. Probe screenshots use the
type-edge filter for readable experimental records. Unit tests verify published
bundle integrity, unsafe links, malformed indexes and derived overview metrics.

U4 review fixed insight footer contrast, blank zero-value plots and responsive
card/control spacing. Full-page screenshots and detail views were reviewed at
both widths and themes; the overview, queue and experiment cards were also
inspected at readable scale.

## U5 landing and routing

The landing page is `/`; the dashboard is `/app`. Screens use real React Router
paths such as `/app/beliefs` and `/app/comparison`, including direct loads and
refreshes. Theme preference persists across page navigation. Deployment: see
"Deploying to Vercel" below.

The landing contains the requested hero, problem bento, numbered process,
required tools, results, CTA and footer. Its stats are verified bundle values.
Any live bundle switches result selection to the live cohort; missing live queue
sides remain pending. Fixture results carry the persistent AGENTS.md banner and
the planted-quirks disclosure. Tool status and purpose are read from the evidence
file. License notices, original registry URLs and adaptation details are in
`docs/CREDITS.md`.

`npm run check:visual` now saves U5 captures to `screenshots/U5`. It includes
landing plus all dashboard pages at both widths and themes, and checks navigation,
deep-link refreshes, theme persistence, missing tool receipts, live result
precedence and visible tamper rejection. The first visual review corrected filled
CTA foreground contrast in both themes. The numbered process and hero anecdote
are user-requested structural/content numbers; measured statistics stay file-backed.

## U6 chart polish

The dashboard now uses Dither Kit's canvas bar and line charts. The line fill uses
step sampling and recorded SVG step connectors, so no intermediate observations
are invented. Unknown values are labelled and withheld from bar painting; zeros
remain explicit. Axis labels use observed values, with fewer ticks when counts
are close. Queue tooltip drops remain signed differences between adjacent counts.
The source and MIT declaration are recorded in docs/CREDITS.md.

Insight and landing CTA cards use the kit's static blue dither gradient over a
dark blue surface. The same Phosphor family supplies chevrons and context icons
for native selects, retaining keyboard/touch behavior. The current visual check
writes artifacts to ignored screenshots/U6 and verifies the queue hover tooltip.

## V2 — Agent Control Center shell

- Routes: `src/routes.tsx` is the single table (path, title, sidebar group, icon, badge,
  parent, element). `/` is the landing page; everything else lives under `/app`. Every
  record has its own URL (`/app/queue/:decisionId`, `/app/probes/:probeId`,
  `/app/beliefs/:beliefId`, `/app/certificates/:certificateId`, `/app/runs/:runId`,
  `/app/reports/:tool`); the selected run is always `?run=<runId>`.
- Data: `src/state/DataProvider.tsx` (`useData()`) loads a local `notary serve`
  (`/api/bundles`, proxied by the dev server to 127.0.0.1:8787) or else the static
  indexes, hash-verifies every bundle, and exposes `{mode, source, runs, runGroups,
  bundles, bundle, baseline, certificates, evidence, loading, error}`. Certificate files are
  validated with the core schema and every seal is recomputed in the browser.
- Primitives: `@/components/ui` (`PageHeader`, `Card`, `KpiCard`, `DeltaPill`,
  `StatusPill`, `FixtureBanner`, `EmptyState`, `LoadingState`, `ErrorState`, `HatchDefs`,
  `HatchSwatch`, sidebar). Shell: `@/components/shell` (`AppShell`, `RunPicker`,
  `CommandPalette` on Ctrl/Cmd+K, `notify` toasts). Tokens: `src/styles.css`.
- `npm run check:visual` iterates every route (`NOTARY_VISUAL=quick` for a short pass).

## V5 — landing page (`/`)

Sections, each number from a data file:

- **Hero** — "Notary issues certificates for API behavior. No certificate, no money moves.",
  dashboard (`/app`) and GitHub buttons.
- **The double-refund problem** (fixture, labelled) — `landing-data.ts` `findIncident` picks the
  first naive decision the grader marked `duplicate` (two write attempts, first timed out) and the
  first marked `wrong_unit` (items[].amount sent vs amount refunded), each with the same request in
  the guarded run (held, missing certificate). Totals are `metrics.unsafe_*`, `executed`, `holds`
  of the fixture naive/guarded bundles.
- **Read → Test → Challenge → Certify → Enforce** — copy mapped to the real modules/commands.
- **Mission control replay** — "Fixture replay — simulated APIs, not a live run". Plays the
  published fixture timelines of one world (its notarize runs, then the guarded run) in a loop,
  each timeline tied to its hash-verified bundle by `bundleHash`. It reuses Mission control's
  `StageGraph`, `stageStats`, `nodeStates` and `edgesForNewEvents` unchanged; the landing adds
  only a looping clock. It pauses off-screen, has a Pause/Play button, and under
  `prefers-reduced-motion` opens paused on the finished state.
- **Required tools** — neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai with status/purpose/notes/links exactly as in
  `public/evidence/evidence.json` (generated by `pnpm notary export --evidence`).
- **Results** — real results from non-sample bundles and `certificates/report.json` ("Not
  measured yet" while there are none); fixture results (labelled) from the fixture bundles and
  `certificates/fixture/<scenario>/report.json`. Never in one table.

## Deploying to Vercel

Config: `packages/web/vercel.json`. Nothing here deploys automatically.

1. Import the GitHub repo in Vercel. **Root Directory: `packages/web`**. Keep "Include files
   outside the Root Directory in the Build Step" **enabled** (the default): the build reads
   `packages/core/src` and the root `pnpm-lock.yaml` / `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
2. Framework preset: **Vite** (vercel.json sets it; its commands override the preset's).
   - Install: `npx --yes pnpm@11.7.0 install --frozen-lockfile` — the root lockfile, the pinned
     pnpm from the root `packageManager` field (no Corepack setting needed); pnpm 11 honours
     `allowBuilds` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, so only esbuild runs a build script.
   - Build: `npx --yes pnpm@11.7.0 --filter @notary/web build` (`tsc --noEmit && vite build`).
   - Output: `dist`.
3. Environment variables: **none required**. Leave `VITE_NOTARY_API` unset on the hosted site.
4. Routing: `/` and `/index.html` are static; `/app` and every `/app/*` deep link rewrite to
   `/index.html`. Everything else is a plain file or a 404.
5. Read-only: there is no `/api/*` on the hosted site (no rewrite, no functions), so
   `GET /api/bundles` is a 404 and the data layer falls back to the static indexes ("static"
   mode). `POST /api/ask` and `/api/approvals` exist only on a local `notary serve`.
6. Caching: `/bundles/*`, `/content/*`, `/certificates/*`, `/evidence/*` are `no-cache` (always
   revalidated, so the in-browser hash checks see the current files); hashed `/assets/*` are
   immutable.

Verified locally (V5) on a clean copy of the working tree (git-tracked + untracked, no
`node_modules`): the install and build commands above succeeded from `packages/web`, and
`vite preview` served `/`, `/app`, `/app/queue/<decisionId>` and `/app/certificates/<id>`
deep links with no page errors. `vercel deploy` itself was not run.

The standalone `packages/web/pnpm-lock.yaml` was removed: nothing used it (the workspace
install ignores it) and it was stale (no @xyflow/react, cmdk or sonner).

# Credits

Third-party code and assets shipped by `packages/web`. Versions are the pins in
`packages/web/package.json`; licenses are the `license` field of each installed package.

## Hook Sidebar (Rare UI)

The guide's table of contents (`/docs`), the dashboard's left navigation and the Run page's
transcript event rail use Rare UI's [Hook Sidebar](https://www.rareui.com/components/hooksidebar),
ported from its source.

| Component    | Source URL                                                                                                                  | Adapted file                       | License                                                   |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hook Sidebar | [rare-ui/components/ui/hook-sidebar.tsx](https://github.com/swamimalode07/rare-ui/blob/main/components/ui/hook-sidebar.tsx) | src/components/ui/hook-sidebar.tsx | MIT + Commons Clause License Condition v1.0 + Attribution |

Where it is used: `src/docs/DocsPage.tsx` (one group per guide section, plus the phone
"Contents" copy), `src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx` (the six pages and the Report link) and
`src/pages/run/Transcript.tsx` (one rail per stage).

Copyright (c) 2026 Swami Malode. The copyright and permission notice are kept in the header of the
adapted file. The required visible credit links [rareui.com](https://rareui.com): "Sidebar
component by Rare UI" at the bottom of the `/docs` sidebar and content column, and "Event rail:
Hook Sidebar by Rare UI" under the Run transcript. The Commons Clause forbids selling or
redistributing the component itself; Notary only ships it as part of the app. Adaptations:
react-router instead of `next/link`/`usePathname`, in-page `#id` items driven by the page's
controlled `value`/`onChange`, an `as="div"` group mode, item badges, `useId()`-based label ids (so
several sidebars on one page never share an id), and Notary token colors (muted inactive rows, ink
active rows, accent rail). The motion springs and reduced-motion handling are unchanged. It needs
`motion` **13.4.6**, pinned exactly.

# @notary/web

The Notary web app: the landing page (`/`), the guide (`/docs`) and the Agent Control Center
dashboard (`/app/*`). React 19, Vite and react-router; one shared UI kit in `src/ui` on the tokens
in `src/design/tokens.css`. The dashboard is light only.

## Pages

| Route                   | What it shows                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/app/run`              | One run step by step: stage stepper, transcript with its event rail, held actions, spend        |
| `/app/certificates`     | Certificates of the selected run's world (active / revoked), claims without a certificate       |
| `/app/approvals`        | Held money actions: decided on a local `notary serve` (Dodo test mode), read-only history otherwise |
| `/app/business`         | Unit economics from real runs; the cfo.ai plan once a plan is imported                          |
| `/app/incidents`        | What went wrong while the agents worked, tied to its neatlogs span and how it was resolved      |
| `/app/chat`             | Questions about runs, certificates and the checked APIs; answers cite records                   |
| `/app/report`           | Run comparison (one world at a time), cost per run, connections and receipts                    |

Every record has its own URL and the selected run is always `?run=<runId>`. Without one, the app
opens a guarded queue run if there is one, else the newest live run that recorded probes or
decisions; replays are never opened first.

## Data rules

- **Every number comes from a data file** in `public/` (run bundles, timelines, certificates,
  incidents, economics, evidence) or from a local `notary serve`. Nothing is hardcoded.
- **Verified in the browser.** Bundles are parsed with the shared zod schema
  (`packages/core/src/schema`) and their `contentHash` is recomputed with
  `packages/core/src/bundle/hash.ts`. Timelines must name their bundle's hash and agree with it
  (probe, decision and certificate counts); the incidents index carries its own `contentHash`.
  Any mismatch withholds the data with a visible error. These two core paths are the only core
  imports.
- **Fixture data is never mixed with real data.** The default view shows real runs only. The
  development view `?fixtures=1` shows fixture runs only, under the banner "Fixture data —
  simulated APIs, not a live run". Each fixture scenario is its own world: counts and tables are
  never summed across scenarios. The synthetic sample bundle (`sample-42`) is in neither view.
- **Replays are labelled.** A replay (`bundle.mode === "replay"`) carries "Replay of
  <original run>" everywhere it is listed, comes after the live runs, and its spend reads
  "Re-served from the recording — no new spend" with the original run linked. Its incidents are
  the original run's and are not counted again.
- **Missing is not zero.** A value nobody recorded reads "Not recorded" or "unknown", never 0.

## Live and hosted modes

- `pnpm --filter @notary/web dev` probes a local `notary serve` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8787`,
  override with `VITE_NOTARY_API`). When it answers, the app is live: starting a run (after a
  confirmation dialog), approving held actions and chat use `/api/*`, which is loopback-only and
  needs the per-session token `notary serve` prints.
- The production build (`pnpm --filter @notary/web build`) is the hosted site: it always replays
  the published files and never contacts a local API.

## Commands

From the repo root (the root `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the only lockfile):

```powershell
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --filter @notary/web dev
pnpm --filter @notary/web typecheck
pnpm --filter @notary/web test
pnpm --filter @notary/web build
```

### Screenshots and the visual check

Both scripts run against a production build served by `vite preview` and use the system Chrome
(Playwright channel `chrome`, no browser download):

```powershell
pnpm --filter @notary/web build
pnpm --filter @notary/web preview --port 5175 --strictPort   # in a second terminal
pnpm --filter @notary/web screenshots    # docs/screenshots/<page>-<width>.png and public/og.png
pnpm --filter @notary/web check:visual   # behavior + layout checks; artifacts in screenshots/K3 (gitignored)
```

`screenshots` captures the landing, the guide and every dashboard page at 1440 and 390 px in the
default (real runs) view, plus a `?fixtures=1` pass (`<page>-<width>-fixture.png`).
`check:visual` checks headings, navigation, deep links, the fixture banner, horizontal overflow,
browser errors and the visible rejection of a tampered bundle. `NOTARY_PREVIEW_URL` and
`NOTARY_SCREENSHOTS` override the base URL and output directory.

## Deploying (Vercel)

Config: `vercel.json`. Root Directory `packages/web`, with files outside the root directory
included in the build (it reads `packages/core/src` and the root lockfile). Install
`npx --yes pnpm@11.7.0 install --frozen-lockfile`, build
`npx --yes pnpm@11.7.0 --filter @notary/web build`, output `dist`. No environment variables are
needed. `/app/*` and `/docs` rewrite to `index.html`; data directories are served `no-cache` so
the in-browser hash checks always see the current files; hashed `/assets/*` are immutable. The
hosted site has no `/api/*`.

## Credits

Third-party components and their licenses: `docs/CREDITS.md`.

An unknown `?run=` falls back to the newest live fixture run.

   - Already in place: distinct ids are counted once, replays are left out, a missing or wrong hash shows a hard "Incidents withheld" error, the "Matches the published bundle" pill comes only from bundles `useData()` verified, the "No trace id recorded" wording is on both pages, and the adversary label comes from `data.verdict`.

Tests cover a dropped verdict, a stray probe, a forged decision, and every published timeline passing.

   - Incidents are counted per fixture scenario.

The index files carry no probe or decision counts, so the choice is made from the verified bundles. Today it opens `notarize-dodo-20261012T012315Z` (15 probes). Tests check this against the published data.
